summary: Flags bars where heavy aggressive volume hit one price while price did not move, and extends that level until a bar closes through it.
overview: Absorption marks bars where a lot of aggressive volume traded but price did not travel far, and the bar closed against the aggressive side. A small marker sits at the absorbed price, and a level line extends to the right until a bar closes beyond it.
Levels where sellers were absorbed (support) are green; levels where buyers were absorbed (resistance) are purple. Broken levels stay on the chart faded, or can be hidden.
how: A bar qualifies when its volume is at least 1.2 times the average of the previous 30 one-minute bars, its volume per tick of range is at least 1.3 times average, and its delta is at least 8% of the bar's volume in one direction while the bar closes the other way.

A level counts as broken when a bar closes beyond it by 2 ticks. Order flow comes from recorded futures trades for NQ, ES, YM, GC, SI and CL (micros use their mini contract's flow) and from public exchange trades for crypto.
use: Some traders watch absorption levels as places where one side met resistance.
Use the faded broken levels to review which absorption levels held.
Some traders combine it with Big Trades to see large orders at the same prices.
notes: Needs per-trade data; other symbols show a note.
It flags past bars; it does not say a level will hold.
